question: Should OpenClaw core own the ordered, authority-preserving startup configuration contract proposed by this PR?
rationale: The implementation is coherent and proven, but permanent ownership of managed configuration composition, immutability, and operator lifecycle semantics is an architecture and product choice that automation cannot make.

options.title: Sponsor bounded core layers
options.body: Approve the generic startup-only contract through the RFC, then require a current-main rebase and refreshed compatibility proof.

options.title: Keep composition external
options.body: Require Lobster and other managed hosts to materialize one canonical config and decline the new public core CLI contract.

options.title: Defer pending RFC consensus
options.body: Leave the draft open without further implementation work until the managed-configuration RFC establishes ownership and scope.

recommendation.title: Sponsor bounded core layers
recommendation.body: Approve the generic startup-only contract through the RFC, then require a current-main rebase and refreshed compatibility proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses core CLI, Gateway startup, configuration authority, and security-sensitive lifecycle behavior represented in this person's recent area history.
